title: Cross-Model SAE Feature Universality: Do Gemma-2 and Llama-3 Learn the Same Features?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Feature universality directly determines whether safety-relevant interpretability findings (deception features, refusal circuits) transfer across models. If universal, one analysis protects many deployments. If not, every model needs independent audit. Highest strategic importance for scalable safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Gemma Scope provides pre-trained SAEs for Gemma-2, reducing one side's cost. However, training or loading SAEs for Llama-3-8B requires more compute. Feature matching via activation correlation on a shared corpus is methodologically well-defined but computationally demanding. Medium compute may be tight for both models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The deliverable (feature universality comparison with category breakdown) is well-defined. However, the full pipeline (load SAEs for both models, run shared corpus, compute correlations, categorize features) has many steps. Could be scoped to a single layer comparison.
